The WCA Delegate contacted with the competitor and the judge and concluded that the time was likely recorded incorrectly.

The Regulations A7b1) states that:
> [A7b1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A7b1)) If penalties are assigned, the judge records the original recorded time displayed on the timer, along with any penalties. (...)

However, the WRC agreed to change the affected attempt to the one that was shown in the tournament display and that only varies in decimal (e.g. XX.X6 to XX.X7).

Generally, incidents regarding recording results from the tournament display follow this policy:

1. The display is visible during a good part of the solve and seems to be working fine.
2. It stops at a believable time (when the competitor stops the timer, + a little delay).
3. The scoretaking mistake is understandable (e.g. The exact time is 10.507 and the judge wrote 10.57. If the display stops at 10.507 and the judge writes 10.53, there is most likely a display error and the recorded time on the scorecard is used).

Please notice that this is not a general ruling and the WRC strongly recommends to write the result directly from the Speed Stacks Stackmat timer. Tournament Displays are not recognized in the WCA Regulations and sometimes, do not match the time of the Speed Stacks Stackmat timer.

entries.title: A Multi-Blind attempt was found to have several misscrambles
entries.content:
A Multi-Blind scheduled second attempt was found to have several duplicate scrambles because of an organizational mistake. The WCA Delegate provisionally changed some certain results to DNF that were surely duplicate scrambles.

The WRC agreed to **change the round format** from "Best of 2" to "Best of 1", because:

1. All second attempts were found to be duplicate scrambles.
2. It is not consistent to disqualify some competitors and not others arbitrarily for an organizational mistake.

This decision involves retroactively removing all second attempts.

entries.title: A Skewb round was found to have several misscrambles
entries.content:
A skewb final was found to have several misscrambles because of an organizational mistake. One scrambler was not familiar with skewb notation and accidentally scrambled wrongly some puzzles.

After analyzing the video evidence, the WRC has concluded the amount of misscrambles significantly affected the final. The WRC agreed to change the round format **from three rounds to two rounds**, because:

1. More than half of the attempts were found to be misscrambled.
2. It is not consistent to disqualify some competitors and not others arbitrarily for an organizational mistake.
3. The misscrambles were found to be noticeably different from the original scrambles.

This decision involves retroactively removing all second attempts. Therefore, the classification was decided with the results from the previous round.

entries.title: 5x5x5 Blindfolded result without a backup stopwatch timing
entries.content:
A competitor solved over 10 minutes in the 5x5x5 Blindfolded event. Due to a miscommunication, the judge did not use a stopwatch assuming that the competitor did not need it.

After analyzing the video evidence, the WRC agreed to **use the original time** because:

1. The time was near to 10 minutes so it was possible to estimate the time from the video.
2. According to [Regulation 9f2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#9f2), the result should be rounded to the nearest second.

In addition, a similar result was accepted at Nacional Perubik 2016 (see [Incident Log](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/6)):

> A competitor got a succesful 5x5x5 Blindfolded solve. The result wasn't written on the score sheet, but the competitor had recorded the solve, so the time was retrieved from the video and the result accepted as official.

entries.title: A competitor signed for the wrong attempt
entries.content:
A competitor signed for the wrong solve attempt. This is considered a DNS according to [Regulation A7c2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A7c2)):

> [A7c2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A7c2)) If the competitor signs (or otherwise marks) an attempt before they have begun it, they forfeit the attempt and the result will be considered DNS.

As the competitor was experienced enough, the [Regulation A7g](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A7g) is not applicable. Therefore the WRC agreed to changed the original attempt to **DNS**.

For the Altona Algorithms Attempt 2 2021 incident, the WRC agreed that this case is substantially different because:

1. The competitor did not do it on purpose.
2. The competitor notified the mistake to the WCA Delegate right after realizing it.
3. It is clear that the competitor knows Article A's procedure and the importance of the signature. The competitor did not attempt to intentionally break the standard procedure not gain an unfair advantage.

Because of this, the WRC agreed to accept the original result for this incident.

The WRC would like encourage competitors to be familiar with the procedure of speedsolving ([Article A](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#article-A-speedsolving)). It is important to understand that the use of the signatures is not arbitrary but rather serves to identify the scramblers and judges and if the competitor agrees with the result.

entries.title: A WDC decision affected a competitor's results on multiple rounds
entries.content:
A competitor had been disqualified after an investigation by the WCA Disciplinary Committee found they were guilty of cheating in a WCA Competition over multiple rounds. Applying [Regulation 2j1a](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#2j1a)), the results of the first round of the competitor should be changed to DNF.

The WRC has decided that the results of the following rounds the competitor participated in should be removed, and not disqualified. [Regulation 9p2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#9p2) states that the competitors who advance to the next round must be determined by ranking or by result in the preceding round. 

Therefore, as the competitor does not have a valid result in the first round, he doesn't meet the requirements for advancing to the next round and should not have competed in it.

The WRC understands that this decision is the best for maintaining consistency of the Regulations. The results should be removed because they were null and void, and not voidable, as they didn't meet the requirements to have happened in the first place.

This is also consistent with the decision taken on [this Incident Log](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/48), in which the WRC decided to remove, and not disqualify, the results of a competitor in a round of an event they shouldn't have competed in due to a mistake they made in a previous round.

As a side effect, this stance could reduce the number of possible competitors that are able to advance to the subsequent rounds due to the [Regulation 9p1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#9p1):

> [9p1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#9p1)) At least 25% of competitors must be eliminated between consecutive rounds of the same event.

As a consequence, some competitors, as has happened in the past, could hypothetically not have advanced to the following round and their results should have been removed.

To prevent those innocent competitors from being harmed by the disqualification of the results of a competitor in an incident they were not involved in, the WRC has agreed to preserve their results, regardless of the number of competitors being able to advance in a previous round.

This is also consistent with the precedent set on [this Incident Log](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/48), as follows:

> More generally, this is what WRC decided to apply when results were wrongly entered, and someone mistakenly proceeded to the next round:
> - Keep the results if the competitor proceeded thanks to an error in someone else's results
> - Remove the results if the competitor proceeded thanks to an error in their own result

As this has become a reoccurring incident, the Regulations will be updated to reflect this understanding of a flexible interpretation of Regulation 9p1 in the special circumstances here described.

Additionally, as this is the first time the WRC has adopted this stance, this understanding should not be applied retroactively, but only on incidents that happen from now on.

entries.title: Proper puzzle covers were not used for a Clock round
entries.content:
Due to a miscommunication, Kharkiv Open 2019 did not have puzzle covers for Clocks on hand. Because of the lack of covers, some judges used a score sheet for the Clock round.

Video evidence confirms that different judges used score sheets during the Clock round. This violates Regulation A2c1:

> [A2c1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A2c1)) The scrambler places a cover over the scrambled puzzle that makes it impossible for any competitors or spectators to see any part of the puzzle. The cover remains over the puzzle until the start of the attempt.

In addition, Guideline A2c1+ explicitly clarifies that paper or score sheets are not an acceptable substitute:

> [A2c1+](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/guidelines.html#A2c1+)) REMINDER In the past, score sheets have been used to cover puzzles while leaving some sides exposed. This is no longer permitted.

Although there is no evidence anyone specifically intended to cheat, this is a serious violation of scramble secrecy. Following the Cavite Open 2 2018 precedent (see [Incident Log](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/31)), the WRC agreed that the **Clock round should be removed**.

entries.title: A competitor was disqualified before their attempts
entries.content:
DISCLAIMER: Since the resolution of this incident, regulation 2j1a has been changed and now allows for results to be entered as DNS rather than DNF, if the competitor has not yet succesfully completed a solve in the round he is disqualified for.

A competitor was disqualified from a round by the WCA Delegate for not doing their judging tasks. Following Regulation 2j1a, the results should be recorded as a DNF:

> [2j1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#2j1)) If a competitor is disqualified from an event for any reason, they are not eligible for any more attempts in the event.
> [2j1a](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#2j1a)) The results of all remaining attempts in the event are recorded as DNF.

However, the WRC found that because the competitor was disqualified before any of their attempts, this fits the definitions of Regulation 9f5 and Guideline 9f5+:

> [9f5](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#9f5)) The result of an attempt is recorded as DNS (Did Not Start) if the competitor is eligible for an attempt but declines it.
> [9f5+](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/guidelines.html#9f5+)) (...). If the competitor did not qualify for an attempt (e.g. in a cutoff round), they have no result for the attempt.

Following the reasoning of BCM Arya Cubing Challenge 2019 incident (see [Incident Log](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/56)) and according to [Guideline 9f5+](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/guidelines.html#9f5+), the WRC agreed that the **competitor's result should be removed**. The Regulations will be updated to clarify this.

entries.title: Use of a 3x3x3 Cube with LEGO Pieces instead of stickers in Fewest Moves Solving
entries.content:
Currently, in Fewest Moves Solving, the stickers can be used as indicators on a puzzle:

> [E3](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#E3)) The competitor may use the following objects during the attempt. Penalty for using unauthorized objects: disqualification of the attempt (DNF).
> [E3c](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#E3c)) Stickers (self-supplied).

Other forms of indicator are allowed as long as the indicators does not break other WCA Regulations. For example, using a 3x3x3 Cube that has tiles that allow blocks (e.g. LEGO blocks) to be placed on them like stickers, is legal as long as it does not break other WCA Regulations. It is okay to use these blocks as indicating pieces by assembling instead of sticking to the puzzle surfaces. 

However, due to [Regulation E3e](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#E3e), the puzzle and the indication pieces should be approved by the WCA Delegates before being used in the Fewest Moves. The WCA Delegate should make sure the puzzles and the blocks are not illegal (e.g. contain electronic aids or might give an unfair advantage).

entries.title: 5x5x5 Blindfolded result missing on the score sheet
entries.content: A competitor got a succesful 5x5x5 Blindfolded solve. The result wasn't written on the score sheet, but the competitor had recorded the solve, so the time was retrieved from the video and the result accepted as official.

entries.title: A runner picked up a popped piece during a competitor's attempt
entries.content:
During a 3x3 round, a piece popped out of a competitor's cube and a first-time runner picked it up and handed it to the competitor, which is not what [Guideline A5b++](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/guidelines.html#A5b++) calls for. An extra attempt was provided by the WCA Delegates because this was the runner's fault and not the competitor's since the competitor did not ask the runner to pick it up and the runner did this by themselves.

The WRC found a DNF to be too harsh for this particular case. As a result, the extra attempt should be used for the following reasons:

1. The extra follows the correct procedure.
2. It was not competitor's fault.
3. The competitor did not attempt to gain an unfair advantage.

In case the original time was available, that original result should have been used. The reasoning for using the original time is to find a compromise between a DNF (which too harsh for something the competitor did not ask for) and an extra (which too kind because the solve with a pop was presumably bad).

entries.title: A competitor's video showed an over-inspected solve without any time callouts by the judge
entries.content:
In a competitor's video for a 3x3x3 Cube attempt, the competitor over-inspected (around 17.1s), but no call outs of 8 or 12 seconds at the correct timestamp were heard in the video.

The initial decision was to DNF this solve, but the decision was overturned by the WCA Board after an appeal. The WCA Board decided that it was more fair to let the result stand.

This was done because of the following:

1. The error was made by the judge and the competitor is not at fault for overinspecting.
2. The competitor may have gained an advantage, but potentially may not have. This is because it is not uncommon for competitors to begin solving when they hear the "8 second" warning, as this competitor did.
3. Because the mistake was made by the judge, an extra should have been provided. However, since an extra was not available, the original time shall stand.
4. A DNF is overly harsh for this situation and accepting the time achieved is more fair.

entries.title: A competitor asked whether ending an attempt with a certain cube state was legal and got an indefinite response
entries.content:
The competitor had two center caps fall off at the end of a 7x7x7 solve. The judge then asked a WCA Delegate whether the competitor had to place the caps on before finishing the attempt, and the WCA Delegate believed that it was fine, but was going to check with the WCA Regulations just to be sure. After the WCA Delegate realized that they were wrong about their initial claim, the competitor had already stopped the timer without the caps on. 

While a provisional extra was provided to the competitor, the solve was deemed a **DNF** because the WCA Delegate initially did not have a definitive answer.

entries.title: A competitor unintentionally caused a misalignment during Megaminx inspection
entries.content:
During the inspection of a Megaminx attempt, the competitor caused an unintentional misalignment to the puzzle, possibly against regulation [A3c1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A3c1).

After careful review of the video footage ([11f](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#11f)), the WRC has decided not to DNF the attempt. None of the frames analyzed point to the face having moved beyond the allowed 36º ([10f2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#10f2)).

entries.title: The "Nod-don" technique was used for Blindfolded Solving (extra not available)
entries.content:
A competitor who used the nod-don technique contacted the delegate after the competition because he thought he may have been close to starting the first turn before the blindfold was fully donned (possibly against regulations [B4a](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#B4a) and [B4b](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#B4b)).

> B4a) The competitor dons the blindfold to start the blindfolded phase.

> B4b) The competitor must not apply moves to the puzzle before they have fully donned the blindfold. Penalty: disqualification of the attempt (DNF).


After analyzing video evidence at full speed, the WRC came to the conclusion that the competitor is not likely to have gained an advantage, thus allowing the solve to remain valid.

entries.title: A competitor used a Clock with a sticker (logo) placed on the side
entries.content:
DISCLAIMER: As of 2025, there is now a specific regulation, regulation [3h4d](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/full/#3h4d), allowing logos to be placed anywhere on the clock, so long as it doesn't obstruct the inner clock faces

A competitor used a Clock with a sticker (logo) placed on the side (different from the flat surfaces of the puzzle).

The puzzle was determined to be competition-legal as per the following arguments:

1. There are no regulations explicitly forbidding logos for Clock puzzles (as long as the logo does not provide any advantage, at delegate's discretion).
2. The WRC concluded that the competitor is not likely to have gained an advantage because of the logo.

entries.title: Square-1 attempt was identified as misscramble (extra not available)
entries.content:
DISCLAIMER: Since the resolution of this incident, the regulation [11i](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#11i) has been updated to provide stricter criteria for when a misscramble should receive an extra.

After the competition, a Square-1 attempt was identified as misscramble.
As an extra was not available and due to the fact that the misscramble was easier than the official scramble, the WRC decided to DNF the attempt.

entries.title: A competitor asked for an extra after stopping the timer
entries.content:
A competitor claimed to be distracted in a 4x4x4 Blindfolded attempt with a DNF result, after finishing the solve, but before finishing the attempt (before signing the score sheet). Delegates granted the competitor an extra attempt as per [Regulation 11e](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#11e).

WRC further discussed this incident and agreed that the **original attempt should stay**. 

When an incident occurs during the attempt, a competitor has three options, each with their own benefits and risks:
1. Immediately stop the attempt and request the extra.
2. Keep the attempt running and appeal for an extra, as per [Guideline 11e+](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/guidelines.html#11e+).
3. Finish the attempt and then try to request the extra.

WRC highly recommends the competitors to choose the first or the second option as the WCA Delegate will be able to better determine the fairness of the appeal and exclude the possibility that the competitor based their request on the result of their solve.

entries.title: Perceptible logos for Blindfolded events
entries.content:
DISCLAIMER: As of 2025, logos are now permitted for 3x3 Blindfolded, but not other blindfolded events per regulation [3l](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#3l)

During the competition, it was noticed that a lot of competitors were using perceptible logos for Blindfolded events. The competitors were asked to remove such logos.

entries.title: Score sheets were used as cube covers in some events of a competition
entries.content:
At Hanoi Open 2022, score sheets were used instead of appropriate cube covers for certain events (Clock, Pyraminx, and Megaminx) in violation of Regulation A2c1:

> [A2c1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A2c1)) The scrambler places a cover over the scrambled puzzle that makes it impossible for any competitors or spectators to see any part of the puzzle. The cover remains over the puzzle until the start of the attempt.

Guideline A2c1+ also explicitly prohibits the use of score sheets as covers:

> [A2c1+](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/guidelines.html#A2c1+)) REMINDER In the past, score sheets have been used to cover puzzles while leaving some sides exposed. This is no longer permitted.

Although there is no evidence that anyone actively tried to cheat, the WRC agreed that this is a serious violation of scramble secrecy, therefore **all the results from Clock, Pyraminx, and Megaminx had been removed**. This decision also follows the precedent from Cavite Open 2 2018 (see this [incident log](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/31)).

entries.title: A competitor should not have advanced to the next round upon the data entry error was found
entries.content:
A competitor qualified for the final round of an event. Upon checking data entry after the final round, but before the competition was over, an error was found which placed this competitor two positions beyond the original advancement conditions. 

The Delegates provisionally decided to change the advancement conditions, increasing the number of competitors qualifying for the final round. Therefore, the competitors affected by this mistake could still compete. The WRC agreed with delegates' decision as per [Regulation 9p2a](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#9p2a) because the decision was in compliance with [Regulation 9p1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#9p1).

entries.title: Timer was reset before the result was recorded (only video evidence showing the display was available)
entries.content:
After a competitor finished their solve, the timer was reset by either the judge (Montpellier Open 2022) or by the timer itself (Bay Area Speedcubin' 29 PM 2022 and Rose City 2022) before the result was fully recorded on the score sheet. The video evidence showed the display but not the timer.

Since the display was clearly shown in the evidence and it was working fine through the solve, WRC agreed that **the original result shown on the display may stand**.

Please note that as per Regulation A7b1 the result must always be recorded from the timer, but not from the display:

> [A7b1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A7b1)) If penalties are assigned, the judge records the original recorded **time displayed on the timer**, along with any penalties...

The time from the display may be accepted when the one from the timer is unavailable **only** under certain circumstances (see the following [incident log](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/51)).

entries.title: A competitor was stopped at the time limit holding a solved puzzle in 3x3x3 Multi-Blind
entries.content:
DISCLAIMER: Since resolution of this incident, clarification [A6e++ ](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/full/#A6e++) was introduced, which provides clarity on how to resolve such an incident.

A competitor was stopped right at the 60 minute time limit in 3x3x3 Multi-Blind holding a solved puzzle. In other words, the competitor was holding the puzzle when the judge stopped the timer, so a time penalty (+2 seconds) was applied following Regulation A6c:

> [A6c](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A6c)) The competitor must fully release the puzzle before stopping the timer. Penalty: disqualification of the attempt (DNF). Exception: If no moves have been applied after stopping the timer and before releasing the puzzle, a time penalty (+2 seconds) may be assigned instead, at the discretion of the judge.

In this case, the competitor was also touching the puzzle after stopping the timer without applying any moves, so another time penalty (+2 seconds) should have been applied as per Regulation A6e2:

> [A6e2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A6e2)) Penalty for touching the puzzle after stopping the timer without applying any moves: time penalty (+2 seconds)...

However, the WRC agreed that: the regulations cited above are unclear regarding the correct way to apply the penalties and the spirit of these regulations is to prevent the competitor from applying moves upon and/or after stopping the timer. Therefore, the attempt was penalized following Regulation A6c only.

entries.title: One piece of the puzzle was found slightly distinguishable after the competition
entries.content:
A competitor contacted the WCA Delegate several days after the competition reporting that one piece of their puzzle had a sound slightly distinguishable from other pieces and that another piece coating  was different from other pieces. Both things were found after the competition. The competitor provided video evidence to show the difference. They used this puzzle during their 3x3x3 Blindfolded attempts. 

The WRC agreed that **the results should be kept as is** for the following reasons:

1. The sound is very lightly distinguishable even in silence, which is not the case in a competitive environment, even during Blindfolded Solving events. 
2. The competitor analyzed the sound difference only after the competition, so there was no defined advantage during the competition. The video of the attempts also showed that the competitor's solving speed could not allow to apply the moves based on the sound and/or texture.
3. The texture was considered reasonable by the WCA Delegate at the competition. Regulation 3j1 allows it:

> [3j2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#3j1)) Puzzles are permitted to have reasonable wear, at the discretion of the WCA Delegate.

entries.title: Scrambles were accidentally reused
entries.content:
A competition staff member competed in 5x5x5 Blindfolded one day prior to the event. Mistakenly, the scrambles that were used for their attempts were reused for one of the next groups. The scrambles were seen by two competition staff members and one competitor who was not competing in that group.

As per Regulation 4b4, the scrambles **should** be applied during a maximum time frame of 2 hours:

> [4b4](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#4b4)) Each scramble sequence should be applied during a maximum time frame of 2 hours. This time frame starts when the scramble sequence is applied for the first time.

The WCA Delegates granted the competitors provisional extra attempts. 

Since scramble secrecy is not guaranteed here and even though Regulation 4b4 wording is "should'', scramble secrecy must be treated seriously. Due to the reasons above, WRC agreed that **the extra attempts should be kept**.

entries.title: A competitor turned off an alarm during a Fewest Moves attempt
entries.content:
During a Fewest Moves attempt a competitor's phone alarm went off. The competitor took out their phone and turned off the alarm. The WCA Delegate confirmed that the competitor used their phone only to turn it off.

Regulation 2i states:
> [2i](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#2i)) While inspecting or solving, competitors must not use electronics or audio equipment (e.g. cell phones, MP3 players, dictaphones, additional lighting) apart from the Stackmat timer or stopwatch.

Additionally, Regulation 2i4 states:
> [2i4](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#2i4)) Competitors should turn off all cell phone notifications while competing to avoid disturbing the competition.

Strictly applying the Regulations, the competitor's attempt must have been disqualified (DNF) as they interacted with their phone (an electronic device). However, the WRC agreed that the attempt should stay for the following reasons:

1. The competitor only turned off the alarm, no advantage was gained.
2. If the alarm continued to be on, other competitors may have been disturbed, which could lead to serious consequences.

The WRC recommends competitors and WCA Delegates to be more careful with electronic devices and to turn them off to avoid similar situations.

entries.title: A judge forgot to hold a sight blocker for a significant amount of time in a 3x3x3 Blindfolded attempt
entries.content:
During Please Be Solved Vancouver 2022 (Jul 24, 2022) and Silver Spring Summer 2022 (Aug 13, 2022), a judge forgot to hold a sight blocker for a significant amount of time in a 3BLD attempt.

In both cases, the decision from the WCA Regulations Committee was to keep the extra attempt. However, in the latter, the decision was overturned by the WCA Board of Directors, thus keeping the original attempt.

The WCA Board of Directors provided the following reasons:
>  1.  No change in the execution speed or positioning of the competitor's head to indicate that they were looking at the cube initially.
>  2.  The speed is in line with the competitor's abilities per previous competitions which were without incidents.
>  3.  It is not the fault of the competitor, but the judge. No actions from the competitor lead to the impression of cheating or even trying to gain an advantage from the situation.

entries.title: Major scramble secrecy and solving procedure issues
entries.content:
Through the years (2013-2022), several Regulations and Guidelines were violated in many competitions in Vietnam. This included:

* Using illegal timers (previous Regulation 8a7, now Regulation 7f1a violated)
* Using score sheets instead of cube covers (Regulation A2c1 and Guideline A2c1+ violated)
* Using Stackmat timers that are not attached to mats (Regulation 7f2 violated)
* Inspection not measured due to missing stopwatches (Regulation A3b2 violated)
* Blank competitor's fields in score sheets (Regulation A7c4 should lead these attempts to be changed to DNF)
* Spectators staying right up against the solving stations (Regulation 7b violated)
* Scrambling area not isolated at all

After investigating each competition based on the delegate reports and publicly available evidence, the  WRC agreed to keep/remove the results based on the following criteria, where removing results supersedes keeping them:

* Competitions using unattached/missing mats - keep results.
* Illegal timers: remove all results from affected competitions.
* Score sheets instead of covers:
  * Prior to 2013, keep all results.
  * 2013 onwards, remove all results from affected rounds.

The decision was approved by the WCA Board of Directors. 

For more details, see [this](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1E-J8WRfld6mpbHslM3rW10fNSsXgkl2y/view?usp=share_link) investigation report and [this](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/posts/wrc-investigation-vietnamese-competitions-results-removal) announcement. See [this](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/70) related incident.

entries.title: EnChroma glasses
entries.content: A mildly colorblind US competitor is trying out special glasses for the colorblind called [EnChroma](http://enchroma.com/) that block out some parts of the color spectrum. It has been decided that these glasses are not likely to offer an unfair advantage, and should be allowed under the current Regulations.

entries.title: Non-permitted timers were used
entries.content:
At Vancouver Island 2019, a Yuxin timer was used during official attempts of several events. The WRC decided to disqualify the rounds where it was used, namely, 3x3x3 Cube, 4x4x4 Cube, 5x5x5 Cube, 3x3x3 One-Handed, and Megaminx.

Per Regulation 8a7 ([2018-01-01](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/history/official/2018-01-01/) WCA Regulations version; now declared by [Regulation 7f1a](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#7f1a)) only Speed Stacks Stackmat timers were allowed to be used at official competitions.

> 8a) An official WCA competition must:
...
8a7) Use the authentic Speed Stacks Stackmat timer (Generation 2, Generation 3 Pro Timer, or Generation 4 Pro Timer) for time measurement.

The main reason for disallowing Yuxin timers is their quality, in particular they sometimes can run with a different speed and measure times incorrectly, which might be not noticeable, especially during fast events.

entries.title: Fewest Moves judge provided wrong information about the WCA Regulations (Delegate unavailable)
entries.content:
During a FMC attempt, the only listed WCA Delegate assigned some of his responsibilities to the judge (the Delegate asked competitors to make questions to the judge), as per [Regulation 1c](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#1c). For this reason, two competitors asked the judge about rotations during the attempt, and both received wrong information. One of the competitors initially got a DNF because of the wrong rotation, and the other one got a DNF regardless of the rotation.

**The final decision was to consider the rotations wrote by the competitors as if they were correct**. Therefore, if the involved competitors wrote z, then the rotation was considered as z', because that is what the competitors would have written if they had received the correct information. The decision from the WCA Regulations Committee had the following reasons (among others explained privately):

1. Although competitors must be familiar with the WCA Regulations as per Regulation [2t](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#2t), the WRC considers that a WCA Delegate (in this case the judge representing the authority of the Delegate) telling wrong information overrides this regulation, in this particular situation.
2. In FMC attempts, delegates and judges **may** give clarifications about the Regulations (see Regulation [E5](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#E5)). If they decide to give clarifications (because they consider that the question is reasonable and they know the answer to the question), the clarification **must** be correct.

entries.title: A competitor went to the bathroom during a Fewest Moves attempt
entries.content:
During a Fewest Moves attempt, a competitor went to the bathroom in the middle of their attempt and returned a few minutes later.

The result was a DNF either way. However, the WRC agreed that it is fine to allow competitors to go to the bathroom during the attempt, as long as the WCA Delegate can ensure that the competitor will not attempt to cheat.

entries.title: A competitor grabbed a microphone during an attempt, to prevent it from falling
entries.content:
DISCLAIMER: Since the resolution of this incident, the [regulation 2i](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#2i) has been updated to provide more insight on what is permitted and not permitted regarding electronic usage.


A competitor was carrying a handheld microphone which was used for announcements during the competition. During a solve he had it lying on the table where it started to roll. He grabbed the microphone to make sure it did not fall off the table. Regulation 2i states:

> 2i) While inspecting or solving, competitors must not use electronics or audio equipment (e.g. cell phones, MP3 players, dictaphones, additional lighting) apart from the Stackmat timer or stopwatch. Penalty: disqualification of the attempt (DNF).

Given that the competitor was not **using** the microphone, he did not break this regulation. The solve was therefore ruled as OK.

entries.title: A competitor uncovered their own puzzle, as the judge failed to do so
entries.content:
DISCLAIMER: Please note that as of 2025, [A2e2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A2e2) explicitly prohibits the competitor from lifting the cover with associated DNF penalty.

> A3b2) The competitor starts the attempt by confirming that they are ready, and the judge uncovers the puzzle and starts timing the inspection.

The competitor said "ready" to the judge before inspection, but the judge did not uncover the puzzle. From a video of the incident, it can be seen that the competitor looks visibly confused and stressed after the judge did not uncover the cube. The competitor then lifted the cover themselves and began the solve shortly after. This was only discovered after the competition, meaning no extras were available. The WRC agreed to keep the original result without penalties, for the following reasons: The procedural error was the judge's fault, the video of the competitor showing he was thrown off by the situation, and no advantage gained (as the inspection time was within 15 seconds).

entries.title: A spectator communicated with a competitor during the competitor's inspection
entries.content:
DISCLAIMER: As of 2025, regulation [A5a](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A5a) has been updated, giving an exception to competitors who do not gain any advantage from their communication.

While the competitor was inspecting the puzzle, a person from the audience asked if they (the competitor) could solve their (the spectator's) puzzle. The competitor responded with "yes, but later". The competitor did not ask for an extra during the attempt. Technically, they communicated with someone other than the delegate and the judge during his attempt, which would be a violation of [Regulation A5a](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A5a).

The regulation, as of February 15th 2023 stated the following:
> A5a) While inspecting or solving the puzzle, the competitor must not communicate with anyone other than the judge or the WCA Delegate. Penalty: disqualification of the attempt (DNF).

The WRC agreed to keep the result as it would be too harsh to DNF it, given that the competitor was just being kind with the young spectator. Furthermore, no advantage was gained from the communication. The regulation was also proposed to be more lenient for the next regulation cycle, to reflect this decision.

entries.title: An attempt was found to be misscrambled by one move
entries.content:
*DISCLAIMER*: Since the resolution of this incident, the regulation [11i](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#11i) has been updated. The outcome of this incident wouldn't change, but how it should be handled is now explicitely stated in the regulations. 

During the competition, after the round was completed, scrambles were verified as a competitor broke a record.

* At Hanoi Super Brain Zyo 2023, one of the attempts in 3x3x3 Cube was found to be misscrambled by the first move of the scramble, affecting only the last move of the solution.
* At Michigan Speedcubing Spring 2023, one of the attempts in Pyraminx was found to be misscrambled by a tip affecting only one move of the solution.

Although the solution was barely affected, and it was similar in difficulty in both cases, the voting among WRC members resulted in a decision to **keep the extra solve** following the standard misscrambles procedure.

entries.title: Attempt was found to be misscrambled after a competition (extra not available)
entries.content:
*DISCLAIMER: The WCA Regulations and Guidelines relating to misscrambles have been updated since this incident was originally published. The approach described below should no longer be followed from January 1st, 2025.*

After a competition, attempts from several competitors were found to be misscrambled. The WRC investigated each of those attempts to determine if they should stay based on the following criteria:

* If the misscramble gives the competitor a significant advantage, the attempt should be changed to DNF.
* If the misscramble is similar in difficulty to the original scramble, the attempt should be left as is.
* If the misscramble cannot be analyzed (e.g. the video of the attempt is not available), the attempt should be left as is.

Please note that in case the misscramble is found during a competition, it must always be replaced with an extra attempt (see the Incident Log entry [here](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/86)).

entries.title: Several rounds were found to have several misscrambles
entries.content:
After a competition, a large number of misscrambles was found to be sent out during certain rounds of several events. In particular, a lot of misscrambles happened during 3x3x3 Cube Final, Pyraminx Final, and 3x3x3 One-Handed Final.

Altghough many attempts during the mentioned rounds were done using correct scrambles, and therefore were valid, the outcome of the internal WRC voting was to **remove all affected rounds** as the number of misscrambles was large. The decision resulted in the removal of 3x3x3 One-Handed event, change in Pyraminx event format from two rounds to one round, and in the change in 3x3x3 Cube event format from three rounds to two rounds. See similar Incident Log entry [here](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/53).

entries.title: Scramble set from the finished group was re-used
entries.content:
After the competition, a competitor reported that they had both the scrambles from the previous group and from their (current) group in their average. The competitor was also a scrambler for the previous group. The WCA Delegate also confirmed they could have left two consecutive scramble sets open at the same time. 

Since the scramble secrecy was violated, the WRC agreed that **the results from the affected round should be removed** (also resulting in the removal of the final round).

entries.title: 3x3x3 With Feet solving without a Mat
entries.content: One competitor was found doing their attempts without a Mat, which was not provided by the organization team for the 3x3x3 With Feet event, and it was disqualified from the event. It was decided that the organization team is responsible to provide the competition equipment, and that the competitor should have been granted extra attempts.

entries.title: Cube covers used for the competition were translucent
entries.content:
WRC received some pictures that showed a cover made of thin white plastic that at some angles could provide some information about the scrambled states of puzzles. However, the WCA Delegates showed the WRC that they had stacked two covers one above the other in order to make them non-translucent and that some single covers were opaque enough to ensure scramble secrecy. 

WRC reviewed the video evidence from the public resources and agreed that the results **should be kept**. While this is not the safest way to cover the puzzles, the organizers and the WCA Delegates did ensure scramble secrecy by double stacking the covers.

### Advice for the Community and Organizers:
Scramble secrecy is an extremely important and delicate matter. If you ever have any concern regarding scramble secrecy during a competition, the safest thing to do is to address the issue with the WCA Delegates of the competition. Breaches in the scramble secrecy may result in the removal of the affected rounds/attempts.

entries.title: Two incidents happened during inspection
entries.content:
During inspection, a competitor reported that their timer was in 4-pad mode. As later discovered, the competitor touched their camera during the inspection violating [Regulation 2i2b](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#2i2b), before reporting the timer issue:

> 2i2b) The competitor must not interact with (e.g. operate, hold, wear) any active camera. Exception: the competitor may wear a camera mounted on their head, as long as it is out of their sight and it is clear that they are not interacting with it (apart from wearing it).

The WCA Delegates granted a provisional extra attempt, but the WRC agreed to **keep the DNF** since the competitor touched the camera **before** reporting the issue with the timer. In general, WRC considers the order in which incidents happen to determine the attempt's result (for example, if the competitor had reported the timer issue first, the extra attempt would have been used).

entries.title: A competitor stopped the official stopwatch in a BLD attempt (judge unavailable to stop it)
entries.content:
DISCLAIMER: As of 2025, regulation [A6a1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A6a1) has been updated, to allow competitors to stop the stopwatch themselves if their judge does not do so.

A competitor finished their attempt and made the signal for the judge to stop the official stopwatch. However, as the judge was unavailable (i.e. too far from the station), the competitor decided to stop the stopwatch themselves (in violation of [Guideline 2i+](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/guidelines.html#2i+)).

Despite the fact that Guideline 2i+ would make this a DNF, **the WCA Regulations Committee agreed to keep the result**, based on the following points:

* **Either the Delegate or the judge saw this situation (key point of consideration for the final decision).**
* [Regulation B5b](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#B5b) was not followed by the judge.
* The competitor had no intention to cheat nor gain an unfair advantage.
* An extra is unnecessarily harsh and mentally draining for Big BLD and MBLD attempts.

entries.title: A 3x3x3 Blindfolded round was found to have several misscrambles
entries.content:
It was reported that several misscrambles were issued during the first round of the 3x3x3 Blindfolded event.
Given the substantial amount of affected attempts, the WRC deemed that the most consistent and fair decision was to remove all the results from the round. As the results were invalidated, it was no longer possible to determine the advancement conditions for the final round. Therefore, the results for any subsequent round were also invalid (and removed).

For more precedents, see the following incident logs: [#53](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/53) and [#88](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/88).

entries.title: A competitor did not fully don the blindfond but was not able to see the puzzle
entries.content:
During 3x3x3 blindfolded attempt, a competitor donned the blindfold in such a way that they were able to see the judge but not the puzzle. The judge said that at some point of the blindfolded phase the competitor looked at them for a few seconds and then continued the execution.

[Regulation B4b](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#B4b) says:

> B4b) The competitor must not apply moves or intentional changes in alignment to the puzzle before they have fully donned the blindfold. Penalty: disqualification of the attempt (DNF).

Since the competitor was able to see the judge and other surrounding, the WRC decided that the blindfold was **not** fully donned, and therefore **the attempt should be changed to DNF**.

entries.title: The judge lifted the cover early and the competitor requested an extra attempt
entries.content:
A competitor called the WCA Delegate asking for an extra attempt, claiming that the judge lifted the cover without him indicating that he was ready. The WCA Delegate granted an extra attempt with the reasoning that no delegates were available at the moment the incident happened (one was competing, one was supervising the scrambling table, and one was outside the room). It was initially thought that the competitor only asked for an extra attempt after the solve was completed. 

The WCA Delegates described their reasoning to the WRC. Initially, the WRC decided to revert the decision of the WCA Delegates and use the original attempt. The WRC based their decision on the following:

* [Regulation 11e](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#11e): "... The competitor should appeal verbally or in writing to the judge and WCA Delegate *at the time of the incident*...".
* [Guideline 11e+++](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/guidelines.html#11e+++): The WRC did not deem the circumstances exceptional enough based on the description of the WCA Delegates.
* [Similar incident](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/incidents/69).

The WRC does not consider the Delegates being temporarily unavailable as an extreme circumstance that would result in an extra attempt. It would be near impossible for a Delegate to reach a competitor within their inspection period. As the incident happened at the very beginning of the inspection, the competitor should have stopped their inspection right away and waited for one of the Delegates to be available to request an extra attempt. 

By following through with the solve, the competitor had the opportunity to decide whether or not they wanted an extra attempt based on their result on the original scramble. This is an unfair advantage that providing an extra attempt in this scenario provides, and this is exactly the reason for 11e+++.

This decision was appealed to the WCA Board. While processing the appeal, new evidence became available - it was found that the competitor did appeal to the judge when the cover was lifted early. The WCA Board decided to overturn the WRC decision, reinstating the extra attempt. The statement from the WCA Board can be found [here](https://forum.worldcubeassociation.org/t/wca-statement-regarding-yiheng-wangs-0-93-2x2-average/49637).
